transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just don’t seem to have the get-up-and-go I used to. I used to like choir, quilting, visiting people… but lately I mostly sit at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time?
I don’t know that I’d call it sad most of the time. I feel kind of… flat, maybe, or just not interested in much. But not crying or feeling empty all day, no.
Do you still enjoy the activities you used to like, such as choir or quilting, when you do them?

Not really. Even if I go, I don’t get much out of it like I used to. With choir or quilting, I just don’t have the push to get started, and most days I end up staying home with the TV on low, even when I know people are expecting me.
Have you noticed any change in your weight recently?
I haven’t really noticed. My clothes seem about the same, far as I can tell.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not really sure. I sleep some nights, and other nights I’m just kind of awake for a while, but I haven’t been keeping track of it.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, nothing in particular comes to mind that I’ve been feeling guilty about.
Do you still find pleasure in the things you used to enjoy?

Not like I used to, no. I used to enjoy choir, quilting, going to visit folks… but lately I just don’t have the push for it. Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know people are expecting me.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than you used to, or have trouble getting started on things?

Yes, I think so. It’s not so much my body is slow, but I just don’t get started like I used to. Choir, quilting, going to see people… I know I should, and folks might be expecting me, but I end up just sitting at home with the TV on low.
Have you been feeling worthless?
No… I don’t think I’d say worthless. I get down on myself sometimes, but not like that.
Do you feel like you're resting or doing things more quickly than you used to?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself doing things faster. Mostly I just feel like I’m doing less, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed myself moving slower, like walking or doing things with my hands. It’s more that I just don’t get going sometimes.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed my clothes getting looser or anything like that.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been going on for a while now. I’d say it started building after I retired from the school office, a little over two years ago.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities and feeling flat are present most of the day?

Yes… most of the day, I’d say. I just don’t have the push I used to. I used to go to choir, do my quilting, visit people, but now most days I sit at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me.
Would you say your feelings of flatness and lack of interest are mild or more severe?

I’d say it’s mild… I mean, it’s there most days, and it keeps me from doing choir or quilting or going to see folks like I used to. But I’m not completely unable to do things. I just don’t have the push anymore.
How many days a week would you say you feel this way?
Most days… probably five or six days a week. I just end up staying home with the TV on low, not really getting to choir or quilting or going to see folks like I used to.
How many months have you been feeling this way?
It’s been a little over two years now, I think. It started building up after I retired from the school office.
Would you say that your lack of interest in activities and feeling flat are interfering with your daily life a lot?

Some, yes. I don’t know if I’d say a lot, but it has changed things. I’ve had to step back from leading choir and helping with projects at the senior center because I don’t keep up with what I said I would do. And my church friends check on me more now than they used to.
Would you say your feelings of flatness and lack of interest are moderate or severe?

I’d say mild, maybe leaning moderate on some days. I’m not completely unable to do things, but I just don’t have the push I used to. Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me for choir or quilting or a visit.
Would you say your lack of interest in activities and feeling flat are causing you significant distress?

Yes, it bothers me. I wouldn’t say I’m falling apart over it, but it’s upsetting to know I used to go to choir and quilting and visit people, and now I just don’t have the push. Most days I’m home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are expecting me.
